input.quote: Garman agrees to indemnify Sparkling and hold it harmless from any and all losses, damages and expenses including without limitation, court costs, arbitration fees, penalties, fines, amounts paid in settlement of claims and reasonable legal fees and expenses of investigation (collectively the "Losses") which Sparkling or any of its respective officers or directors may incur due to a breach of this warranty.
input.rationale: Section 13 contains a Vendor-side IP indemnity: Garman warrants it owns or controls all rights necessary to grant the licence and free of liens, and indemnifies Sparkling (and its officers and directors) for all Losses, including settlement amounts and legal fees, arising from breach of that warranty, backed by the usual infringement remedies of procuring rights, procuring an equivalent element, or replacing/modifying the Work (p0091–p0093). Section 15 expressly carves breaches of Section 13 out of the liability limitation, so the indemnity is uncapped and better than the fallback's 3x-fees super-cap. No indemnity runs from Sparkling to Garman anywhere in the Agreement, so there is no one-sided or broad Customer indemnity to narrow. The clause therefore meets the fallback (and much of the preferred) position on its material terms. Noted but not flagged as deviations: no express duty to "defend" or allocate defence control, no refund remedy if the infringing element cannot be cured, the ten-calendar-day claim notice is tighter than we would prefer, and the non-IP heads (Vendor breach of law, Vendor-caused data breach, gross negligence/wilful misconduct) are absent from the preferred position.
